### Defs and `call`

- `defs`, when present, must be an object whose keys match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` and whose values are `{"steps": [...]}`. Its structure is checked right after the other top-level fields. Then the main pipeline steps are normalized, then each def's steps in declaration order, and the recursion check runs last.
- `call.name` is matched exactly (no trimming, case-sensitive). An invalid name is `SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED`; a valid name with no matching def is `UNKNOWN_DEF` at `.name`. A null `params` is the same as a missing one. A parameter value that is (or contains) an object is `SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED` at `.params.<key>`.
- No call cycles are allowed anywhere, including between unused defs. The search starts from the main pipeline and then covers the remaining defs in order. The call that closes the cycle is reported at its `.name` path, e.g. `defs[Loop].steps[0].name`.
- Each call binds its own `params` only; a nested call doesn't inherit the caller's params. An unbound `params.key` (including any use in the main pipeline) is null. A bare `params`, or `.` member access on anything else, is `BAD_EXPR`.
- Errors raised while a def runs use `defs[Name].steps[k]...` paths.
EOF
